method.heap: Separate Chromium forced-GC diagnostic: awaited producer pause after indexed pages 1/100/500/1000; exact same isolate heap before/after HeapProfiler.collectGarbage for the parser and for every other identified live isolate (extractor, storage worker, page). Collection and pause included in timings; post-GC observation is not a hard bound or peak.
method.timingClassification: Instrumented forced-GC diagnostic: producer pauses and collection costs included; not production performance
method.browserLaunch: launchPersistentContext; fresh profile per case; browser PID is the unique new live direct child of this runner
method.postExtractionObservation: Outside totalExtractionMs: ten foreground reads spaced100ms apart, two timed public searchStatus reads, and advisory search notification count. Queue-inclusive latency; no isolated background SQL CPU attribution.
method.rss: 500 ms ps browser-server process-tree RSS. Includes browser/storage/PDF workers and shared pages (which may be counted more than once); excludes reparented or OS-managed processes. Sampling misses brief peaks. Not parser heap, physical memory, or a hard memory bound. Runner/OS file caches are outside this process-tree measure.
method.foreground: Bounded public readEntities(document,1 item,8192 bytes), dispatched immediately after real publishExtractionPage without awaiting its reply. First page and every tenth page. Queue-inclusive latency, observer overhead included. Baseline: ten reads immediately before extraction.
method.limits: 32 MiB source cap; PDF.js may allocate whole source, decompressed structures and page arrays. No production heap guarantee. Single synthetic run per case is diagnostic, not a release threshold or controlled distribution.
